quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Use the brake throughout the turn.

questions.explanation: You should change gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Make it hard to see road hazards.
Invite other vehicles to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other vehicles and lets them see you. Avoid staying in another driver's blind spot.

questions.question: To avoid crashes, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you and understand what you plan to do. Use proper signals and lane positioning. Keep space around you and watch for hazards ahead.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection to:

options.text: See if parked vehicles are entering traffic.
Check for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
See if someone plans to turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, check your mirrors for vehicles approaching from behind. Drivers may not see you until they are close, so you need to be ready to react.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for at least an hour.
After riding for more than 8 hours.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes of starting to ride.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up rather than to steer.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to maintain balance during turns. Sit so your arms steer rather than hold you up. Sit far enough forward that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if turning too fast.
Can take any turn at any speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if turning too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a sidecar can tip if you turn too sharply or go too fast for the turn.

questions.question: When you ride a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following except:

options.text: How much tread is on your tires.
The general condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tire tread wear, and the overall condition of your tire sidewalls and tread.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, what happens to acceleration and stopping?
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle slower to speed up and slower to stop.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know they see you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield just because they made eye contact with you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but do not notice them.

questions.question: Your body eliminates one alcoholic drink per hour. Someone drank eight drinks four hours ago. How many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: Drivers merging onto the highway from a ramp on your right may not see you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it.
Move into another lane, if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if needed.
questions.explanation: Give vehicles plenty of room when they merge from an entrance ramp. Change lanes away from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them space to merge safely.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: When you need to stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Which of these should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam headlight when no other vehicles are nearby, and stay farther back from other vehicles. Watch the vehicles in front of you—their lights help you see the road ahead and show if there are bumps.
